# trust-ui-react

> A mobile-optimized, themeable React UI library: CSS Modules, CSS-variable tokens, no runtime styling. Install `trust-ui-react`, import `trust-ui-react/styles.css` once, and import components by name.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/getting-started/installation): npm install trust-ui-react
- [Localization](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/getting-started/localization): Some strings are produced by the components themselves rather than passed in by you: accessible names (Close dialog, Next page), empty states (No options found) and built-in button labels. LocaleProvider sets their language.
- [Migrating from v1](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/getting-started/migration-v1-to-v2): Almost every breaking change between v1 and v2 fails to compile. elevation, gradient, size, variant, zebra, and the mobileVariant="stacked" value are gone from the component types — TypeScript, or your editor, will stop you at every call site that used them. Fix those and you're done with them.
- [Theming](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/getting-started/theming): trust-ui v2 theming is plain CSS custom properties keyed off a handful of data-* attributes on <html>. There is no runtime color computation — nothing derives a hover shade or a tint from a base color for you. Every state a component can render has to resolve to a token that's actually defined somewhere in the cascade.

## Components

- [ActionSheet](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/action-sheet): A pre-styled action picker built on top of BottomSheet. Renders a vertical list of buttons with optional title and Cancel — modeled after iOS UIActionSheet. Use it when the user needs to pick one action from a short list (3-6 items), typically as a "more actions" or "share" picker.
- [AvatarGroup](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/avatar-group): Stacks avatars so they overlap, and collapses the ones that do not fit into a "+N" tile.
- [Avatar](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/avatar): Displays a user image, initials fallback, or a default icon.
- [Badge](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/badge): A small label used to highlight status, counts, or categories.
- [Banner](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/banner): A persistent message at the top of a page or section. Unlike a Toast, it stays until the condition it describes is resolved or the user dismisses it.
- [BottomNav](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/bottom-nav): A bottom bar for switching between the 2–5 top-level destinations of a mobile app. It is navigation, not a set of tabs: for switching panels inside one screen use Tabs.
- [BottomSheet](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/bottom-sheet): A bottom-anchored modal panel native to mobile UX. Supports multiple snap points, drag-to-resize, swipe-to-dismiss, and backdrop tap dismiss. Use it for filter panels, detail pages, comment lists, action confirmations — anywhere a centered modal would feel out of place on touch.
- [Breadcrumbs](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/breadcrumbs): Shows where the current page sits in a hierarchy and links back to each ancestor.
- [Button](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/button): A clickable button with multiple variants, sizes, shapes, and loading state.
- [Calendar](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/calendar): A standalone calendar grid used internally by DatePicker and DateRangePicker. Can also be used independently to display a month view.
- [Card](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/card): A surface for one discrete item: an account, a report, a plan. A card can be a plain container, a single link or button, a container with a stretched title link, or a selectable option.
- [Carousel](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/carousel): Horizontally swipeable slides. The track is a native scroll container with CSS scroll snapping, so touch momentum, trackpads and keyboard scrolling behave as they do everywhere else on the platform. JavaScript only tracks the current slide and scrolls for the buttons.
- [Checkbox](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/checkbox): A toggle control that allows users to select one or more options.
- [Chip](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/chip): A compact element for tags, filters, or selections. Supports delete and click actions.
- [Combobox](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/combobox): A searchable single-select where the user types freely and picks from a filtered list. Use it for long or server-backed lists; for a short static list, Select with searchable is enough.
- [DatePicker](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/date-picker): A date input with a popup calendar for selecting a single date. Supports year navigation and date constraints.
- [DateRangePicker](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/date-range-picker): A date input for selecting a range of dates. Displays two side-by-side calendars and supports preset ranges.
- [Dialog](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/dialog): A modal dialog overlay for confirmations, forms, or important content. Built on the native <dialog> element.
- [Divider](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/divider): A hairline that separates sections of content or items in a row.
- [Drawer](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/drawer): A full-height modal panel that slides in from the side of the screen. Use it for detail views, filters and edit forms that should keep the page behind in context. For a short confirmation use Dialog; for a thumb-reachable panel on phones use BottomSheet.
- [EmptyState](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/empty-state): A placeholder for an area that has no data yet — an empty list, a search with no results, a feature that has not been set up.
- [Expander](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/expander): An accordion component for collapsible content sections. Supports single and multiple expansion modes.
- [Field](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/field): A low-level shell that gives any custom control a label, helper text, a required marker and an error message, with the ARIA wiring done for you. NumberInput, Combobox and TimeInput are built on it. Reach for it when you wrap a control the library does not provide.
- [FileUpload](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/file-upload): A file upload component with drag-and-drop support, file validation, and preview functionality.
- [Grid](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/grid): A CSS grid layout primitive. By default it is responsive without media queries: it fits as many columns as the container allows and collapses to a single column when space runs out.
- [IconButton](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/icon-button): A button that shows only an icon. It takes the same variants, sizes and shapes as Button, and always requires a text label.
- [KeyboardAvoidingView](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/keyboard-avoiding-view): A container that adds bottom padding equal to the on-screen keyboard height when the keyboard is open. Use it for chat input rows, multi-step forms, and any layout that must stay visible above the keyboard.
- [List](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/list): Rows for settings screens, menus that are pages, and simple collections. It is the narrow-screen counterpart of a table: one item per row, a title, an optional description, and a slot at each end.
- [Menu](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/menu): A dropdown menu triggered by a button click. Supports keyboard navigation, disabled items, and dividers.
- [NumberInput](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/number-input): A numeric field with keyboard stepping, range clamping and optional locale formatting. The value is a number (or null when empty), not a string.
- [Pagination](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/pagination): Navigation controls for paging through data. Supports numbered pages and a simple previous/next variant.
- [Popover](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/popover): A click-triggered overlay anchored to its trigger, for secondary content: an explanation, a short form, a handful of options. It is non-modal — the page behind stays usable. For a list of actions use Menu; for a hover hint use Tooltip; for a task that must be finished or dismissed use Dialog.
- [Progress](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/progress): A horizontal bar that indicates the completion of a task or process.
- [Radio](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/radio): A set of mutually exclusive options. Use RadioGroup to wrap multiple Radio components.
- [SafeAreaView](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/safe-area-view): A layout primitive that applies env(safe-area-inset-*) padding to its edges. Use it at the root of fullscreen mobile screens, custom modals, and any element near the iOS notch (top) or home indicator (bottom).
- [SegmentedControl](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/segmented-control): A compact, equal-width control for switching between 2-4 mutually exclusive options. Inspired by iOS UISegmentedControl — ideal for view toggles, filter sets, and grouped selectors where Radio would feel too loose and Tabs too heavy.
- [Select](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/select): A dropdown component for selecting one or more options from a list. Supports search, multi-select, and keyboard navigation.
- [Skeleton](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/skeleton): A placeholder that mirrors the shape of content while it loads. Use it when you know the layout that is coming (a list row, a card, a paragraph); use Spinner when you do not.
- [Slider](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/slider): A range input for selecting a numeric value within a given range.
- [Spinner](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/spinner): An indeterminate loading indicator for content whose shape or duration is not known. When the layout is known, prefer Skeleton; when progress is measurable, prefer Progress.
- [Stack](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/stack): A flexbox layout primitive that spaces its children with a step from the spacing scale. Use it instead of hand-written display: flex wrappers so every gap in the app comes from --tui-gap-1 … --tui-gap-6.
- [StatusDot](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/status-dot): A small dot that shows presence or severity next to a name, a row or a heading.
- [Stepper](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/stepper): Shows progress through a sequence of numbered steps. Steps before activeStep are complete, the active one is current, the rest are upcoming.
- [StickyFooter](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/sticky-footer): A sticky bottom container with thumb-zone-safe padding and built-in safe-area handling. Use it for primary CTAs in mobile forms (e.g., "Continue" at the bottom of a wizard, "Save" on an edit screen) — always reachable by the thumb.
- [Switch](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/switch): A toggle switch for binary on/off states.
- [Table](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/table): A data table with sorting, custom cell rendering, a total row, and a narrow-viewport summary layout.
- [Tabs](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/tabs): Organizes content into tabbed sections. Supports underline and pill variants with keyboard navigation.
- [TextArea](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/text-area): A multi-line text input that grows with its content, with an optional character counter. It shares its label, helper text, error wiring and surface with the other fields.
- [TextField](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/text-field): A versatile text input supporting labels, helper text, validation, passwords, multiline, and number formatting.
- [TimeInput](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/time-input): A time-of-day field. The value is always a 24-hour 'HH:mm' string (or null), whatever clock is displayed.
- [Toast](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/toast): A notification message that appears temporarily to provide feedback about an action.
- [Tooltip](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/tooltip): A popup that displays informative text when hovering or focusing on a trigger element.
- [VisuallyHidden](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/components/visually-hidden): Text that is invisible on screen but still read by screen readers. Use it to name icon-only controls, add context that sighted users get from layout, or keep a heading in the document outline without showing it.

## Guides

- [Accessibility](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/guides/accessibility): What the components do for you, what stays your job, and the keys each widget responds to.
- [Layers](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/guides/layers): trust-ui v2 ships as one required stylesheet plus a small set of optional layers you turn on only if your product needs them. This page is the entry point: answer the questions below about your own product, and each answer tells you exactly what to import or set — nothing more.
- [Mobile patterns](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/guides/mobile-patterns): trust-ui v2 is mobile-optimized, not just responsive: several of its rendering decisions depend on which *pointer* is in use, not just how wide the viewport is. This guide covers the mechanics — density vs. pointer, how Table behaves under 640px, safe areas, horizontal scroll, and why form inputs never trigger iOS's auto-zoom.

## Design tokens

- [Colors](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/design-tokens/colors): trust-ui v2 splits color into three layers. Each layer has exactly one job, and components only ever read from the last one.
- [Elevation](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/design-tokens/elevation): trust-ui v2 has exactly one shadow.
- [Motion](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/design-tokens/motion): trust-ui v2 motion answers user actions. It does not decorate.
- [Spacing & Radius](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/design-tokens/spacing): Spacing splits into two independent scales — one tied to density, one fixed — because they answer two different questions.
- [Typography](https://trustspirit.github.io/trust-ui-react/docs/design-tokens/typography): trust-ui v2 sets one typeface — Pretendard — for everything: UI chrome, body copy, and numeric figures alike. There is no separate mono stack and no second brand face.
